territorial_scope.description: Federal U.S. bill directing federal agencies (DOE, DOT, NIST) and federal funding for projects, enacted by the United States Congress.

evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

summary.short: Proposed federal bill authorizing Department of Energy grants for demonstration projects on next-generation pipeline technologies, a joint DOE, DOT and NIST research program, a National Pipeline Modernization Center and NIST pipeline metrology funding, with appropriations authorized for fiscal years 2026 to 2030.
summary.long: The bill would add section 40344 to the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, authorizing the Secretary of Energy to award financial assistance to eligible entities for low- to mid-technology-readiness demonstration projects on pipelines, LNG facilities and gas and liquid fuel storage. Eligible entities include universities, nonprofit research organizations, National Laboratories and private commercial entities. Listed focus areas include leak detection, sensors, machine learning models and cybersecurity. Section 40344 authorizes $45,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 and $50,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030, drawn from section 10771 funds, and terminates five years after enactment. Section 5 directs a joint DOE, DOT and NIST research program, subject to appropriations. Section 6 directs a National Pipeline Modernization Center, run with a competitively selected eligible entity for up to five years. Section 7 directs NIST pipeline measurement research with up to $2,500,000 per fiscal year for 2026 through 2030. Section 8 authorizes appropriations for Sections 5 and 6 and amends section 10771 funding amounts. The bill is pending.

thresholds.note: This bill authorizes appropriations and creates R&D programmes (sections 4-8). Its dollar figures are authorizations of appropriations (sections 4(e), 7(c), 8(a)) and funding offsets (section 8(b)), not cutoffs that change legal treatment. The five-year sunsets (sections 4(f), 5(h)) and the agreement period of not more than five years (section 6(d)) are time limits, recorded as events or not thresholds. No scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty or price tier is set by a numeric value.
